chunks: Aban, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Al-Abbas Al-Makki, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Umar met the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'You are the one who recites this Verse: 'Which of you is afflicted with madness', applying it to me and my companion.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I not inform you of a Verse which descended regarding the Clan of Umayya?'
But if you held command, you were sure to make mischief in the land and cut off the ties of kinship!
So he said, 'You are lying. The Clan of Umayya establish more ties of kinship than you do, but you are most insistent upon enmity to the Clan of Taym and Udayy, and the Clan of Umayya.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.بَنِي تَيْمٍ: Clan of Taym (tribe of Abu Bakr)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the verse 'Which of you is afflicted with madness' in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this notable encounter, Umar ibn al-Khattab challenges Imam Ali (as) on whether he applied the verse 'Which of you is afflicted with madness?' (68:6) to himself and Abu Bakr; Imam Ali counters by citing the verse regarding the cutting of kinship ties (47:22), specifically linking it to the Banu Umayya. This exchange highlights the Shia scholarly view that while Umar may have been technically correct in his kinship ties, his persistent enmity toward the Banu Taim and Banu Umayya demonstrated a spiritual severance, contrasting with Imam Ali's unwavering connection to the Prophet's household.
